meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 15 (Multi-Select): Versioning, 2026-07-28 Changelog & Feature Lifecycle
meta.format: multi_select: questions use the 'answers' array (multiple correct options). Some include an 'All of the above' option that is only correct when every other option is.

questions.question: Which features are DEPRECATED (not removed) as of 2026-07-28? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Roots
Sampling
Logging (notifications/message)
The legacy HTTP+SSE transport
The ping method

questions.explanation: Roots, Sampling, Logging (SEP-2577) and HTTP+SSE (SEP-2596) are Deprecated with at least a twelve-month window. ping was removed outright, not deprecated.

questions.question: Which are MAJOR changes in the 2026-07-28 changelog? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Removal of protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header
Removal of the initialize handshake in favor of per-request _meta
Addition of the mandatory server/discover RPC
Replacement of the HTTP GET endpoint and resources/subscribe with subscriptions/listen
A switch of the wire format from JSON to CBOR

questions.explanation: A–D are all listed major changes (SEP-2567/2575), alongside MRTR, resultType, the Tasks extension move, and SSE resumability removal. The wire format remains JSON-RPC 2.0.

questions.question: Which authorization changes landed in 2026-07-28? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Authorization servers SHOULD include iss in authorization responses, and clients MUST validate a present iss before redeeming the code
Clients MUST specify an appropriate application_type during Dynamic Client Registration
Credentials are bound to their issuing authorization server — persisted per issuer, never reused across servers
Dynamic Client Registration was deprecated in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents
PKCE was removed as unnecessary

questions.explanation: All four hardening changes are in the changelog (SEP-2468, SEP-837, SEP-2352, and the DCR→CIMD deprecation). PKCE remains a core requirement of the OAuth 2.1 flow.

questions.question: Which statements about the feature lifecycle and deprecation policy are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Features move through Active, Deprecated, and Removed states
The minimum deprecation window is twelve months
Deprecated features keep working in this version and every version published within a year of it
Actual removal requires a separate, explicit proposal
Deprecated features stop working on the release date

questions.explanation: SEP-2596's policy: three states, a 12-month minimum window, continued function during it, and removal only via a separate proposal — so nothing broke on July 28.

questions.question: Which things did 2026-07-28 REMOVE outright (rather than deprecate)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The ping method
logging/setLevel (log level moved to per-request _meta)
notifications/roots/list_changed
SSE stream resumability (Last-Event-ID)
The Sampling feature

questions.explanation: Sampling is deprecated (12-month window), not removed. The other four are gone from the modern era.

questions.question: Which error-code moves happened in the 2026-07-28 renumbering? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: HeaderMismatch: -32001 → -32020
MissingRequiredClientCapability: -32003 → -32021
UnsupportedProtocolVersion: -32004 → -32022
Resource not found: -32002 → -32602 (aligning with JSON-RPC Invalid params)
All of the above

questions.explanation: All four renumberings are in the changelog, following the new allocation policy reserving -32020..-32099 for the spec.

questions.question: Which statements about protocol eras are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Legacy = initialize handshake, protocol versions 2025-11-25 and earlier
Modern = per-request protocol metadata, 2026-07-28 and later
Dual-era implementations deliberately support both styles
A modern-only client can interoperate with a legacy-only server because negotiation bridges the gap
All of the above

questions.explanation: Negotiation only DETECTS the mismatch; bridging requires an actual dual-era implementation. D is the classic misconception.

questions.question: Which governance changes shipped with 2026-07-28? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A feature lifecycle policy with Active, Deprecated, and Removed states (SEP-2596)
A minimum twelve-month deprecation window plus a deprecated-features registry
A formalized PR-based SEP workflow with markdown files, sponsors, and label-driven status (SEP-1850)
A rule that deprecated features silently stop working after six months
All of the above

questions.explanation: Six-month silent breakage is the opposite of the policy: features work for at least twelve months and removal needs its own proposal.
